messages:
maya_patel: Hi all 010first week! I accepted the org invite but when I try to clone or push to repo 'redwood-inference/infra' I get a 403. I can see the repo list in the web UI but the clone fails with permission denied. Anyone know who to ping? :confused:
onboarding-bot: Welcome @maya_patel! Common causes: not yet mapped to the repo team, SSO not linked, or GitHub 2FA enforcement. Ping @it-support with the invite email.
maya_patel: I used maya@companymail.com for the invite. Git push error: "remote: Permission to redwood-inference/infra.git denied to maya_patel. fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/': The requested URL returned error: 403"
it-support: Thanks Maya. Can you confirm: did you complete SSO sign-in when you accepted the invite? Also does your GH account have 2FA enabled?
maya_patel: I completed SSO during acceptance. 2FA is enabled (auth app). I can view some repos but not infra.
ben_dev: Sounds like a team mapping issue. Infra is only accessible to members of team infra-ops (permission: write). Org uses SCIM group sync so you need to be in that team. @rebecca can you check if maya is in infra-ops?
rebecca: Checking... Maya is in default "engineering" group but not infra-ops. Normally we auto-map from GSuite groups but this one didn't sync. I'm going to add you manually now.
rebecca: Done - added maya_patel to infra-ops. You might need to log out/in or run git credential helper to refresh creds.
maya_patel: Re-cloned and now clone works, but push still 403 when I try to push a branch. Git remote shows: origin https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra.git (fetch/push)
it-support: Try clearing cached credentials: ``git credential-cache exit`` or on mac: ``git credential-osxkeychain erase`` and then try push so Git re-prompts for SSO OAuth flow. Also check that PATs aren't being used (we require SSO auth).
maya_patel: Ran the erase command, retried push, it now redirected to SSO and I authorized, push succeeded. Thanks! :tada:
deploy-bot: Automated: added maya_patel to team infra-ops, updated repo ACLs. If you need deploy-runner access open a ticket in #eng-infra.
rebecca: Welcome again @maya_patel. If anyone else hits the weird "see repo but 403 on push" flow, it's usually a team mapping or cached credential (PAT) issue. Short checklist: 1) confirm SSO, 2) verify team membership, 3) clear cached creds.
